Read a DynamX cluster or state data export

Source: R/read_hdx.R
read_dynamx.Rd

Converts a Waters DynamX export to the HDXBoxeR input table.

Usage

read_dynamx(
  path,
  type = c("auto", "cluster", "state"),
  fd = NULL,
  protein = NULL,
  combine_charges = FALSE
)

Arguments

path

path to the csv file.

type

"auto" (default), "cluster" or "state".

fd

how the fully deuterated control is identified: NULL (default, none), the name of a DynamX State holding the control (its measurements become the "FD" control of every other state), or "last" to use each state's longest exposure as its control (that exposure is then not kept as a time point).

protein

which DynamX Protein to keep when the file holds more than one. Default: all (an error if there are several).

combine_charges

FALSE (default) keeps every charge state as its own peptide, as for HDXExaminer input. TRUE combines charge states of a peptide into one intensity-weighted mass per raw file (as in the DynamX state export).

Value

data frame of class hdx_data.

Details

Cluster data (one row per peptide, state, exposure, raw file and charge; DynamX 2.x or 3.x): each raw File is a replicate. Center is the centroid m/z, so the neutral mass is z * (Center - proton mass). Uptake of a replicate is its mass minus the mean mass of the undeuterated (Exposure 0) measurements of the same peptide, charge and state. Percent deuteration is 100 * uptake / MaxUptake.

State data (one averaged row per peptide, state and exposure): Uptake is used directly as a single measurement per time point. It contains no replicates, so functions that need replicate SDs or t-tests cannot use it; a warning says so.

Exposure is in minutes in DynamX and is converted to seconds (time labels such as "600.00s"; times of 1 s or more are rounded to whole seconds, so 0.167 min becomes "10.00s"). Very short "in-exchange" controls (e.g. Exposure 0.001 min) are kept as a time point; leave them out with the times argument of output_tp(). Note that DynamX's MaxUptake counts exchangeable amides as length - 1 - prolines, while HDXBoxeR's nb_exch_deut() uses length - 2 - prolines.
